text:
alex-docs: Heads up — I found a mismatch in the fallback example for embed sharding between the model card and the SDK snippet. model-card shows `nebula3b-quant-v2` while the SDK example uses alias `nebula3b`. That breaks fallback in Private when prefix_cache=false.
chris-sdk: Can you paste the exact lines? I vaguely remember the SDK examples used aliases to keep them short.
alex-docs: Sure — from the SDK snippet in docs:
```python
from redwood import Client
c = Client()
resp = c.embed('some short text', model='nebula3b')
```
and from the model card example:
```yaml
supported_variants:
  - nebula3b-quant-v2
  - nebula3b-quant-v1
```
maria-ml: We added alias -> variant auto-mapping in the runtime last month, but that mapping only exists in Hosted. Private/air-gapped deployments don't get the alias registry by default — so passing alias can be an incompatible request there.
pat-platform: Is this limited to embeddings or could it affect generate/chat as well? If Private doesn't have alias mapping, any example using alias could mislead customers. I suggest we: (1) update the model card example to show explicit variant name for Private, (2) add a short callout about alias registry differences, and (3) update the SDK snippet to show `Client.resolve_variant()` as a fallback helper.
alex-docs: Agreed. I'll prepare a PR that updates the model-card example to demonstrate the explicit variant and add a Private note. For the SDK snippet I plan to show an explicit resolve pattern, e.g.:
```python
# prefer explicit variant in private deployments
variant = c.resolve_variant('nebula3b')  # returns 'nebula3b-quant-v2' when available
resp = c.embed('text', model=variant)
```
or the more defensive pattern:
```python
try:
  resp = c.embed('text', model='nebula3b-quant-v2')
except IncompatibleVariantError:
  resp = c.embed('text', model='nebula3b-quant-v1')
```
chris-sdk: :thumbsup: showing `Client.resolve_variant` is a good call. We already expose that helper; link it to the SDK reference (`/sdk/reference#resolve_variant`). Also add a short comment about fallback semantics across deployment types.
doc-bot: Note — link placeholder: https://github.com/redwood/inference-sdk/docs/resolve_variant (to be replaced with canonical URL before merge)
ci-bot: PR #5421 opened by alex-docs: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/5421 — "model-card: clarify variant examples and Private alias behavior"
pat-platform: Can we also add a small docs smoke test to ensure example snippets are syntactically correct and links resolve? If the snippet runs as a minimal unit test (with a mocked client) it would catch regressions.
chris-sdk: I'll add a tiny test in the examples repo to import the snippet and call `Client.resolve_variant` with a mocked registry. Will submit a follow-up PR against sdk-examples.
maria-ml: One more ask: please add a one-line note on the benchmarks page that alias resolution/alias registry availability is a deployment difference and does not affect the reported per-variant throughput numbers — just a compatibility/runtime mapping detail.
alex-docs: OK — I'll fold that into PR #5421. ETA end of day. @chris-sdk would you be able to review once it's up? @pat-platform please confirm the ops note wording is fine.
chris-sdk: Reviewing now, leaving small nits.
alex-docs: Fixed nits and updated the resolve_variant link to point to the SDK ref. CI green :white_check_mark:
ci-bot: PR #5421 merged by alex-docs — https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/5421
pat-platform: Thanks all. Can someone add a one-line release note for the docs change so our internal KB and release notes include the Private behavior callout?
alex-docs: Will add release note in the docs CHANGELOG after lunch.
maria-ml: Great — closing the loop. If we see more alias-related confusion, we should consider a short KB article on alias registry and migration for Private customers.
chris-sdk: Agreed. I'll draft a short how-to for SDK examples repo on resolving variants and linking to model cards.
alex-docs: Thanks — appreciate the quick turn. :rocket:
